data.user_prompt: Which crawlers should a website allow for AI search, and which can it block?

sections.text:
For **AI search visibility**, a website should generally **allow the search/retrieval crawlers** that power citations and live answers, while **blocking the training crawlers** if it does not want its content used to train models.[4][11][17][20]

A practical default is:

| Allow for AI search | Common purpose | Block if you want to prevent training |
|---|---|---|
| **OAI-SearchBot** | ChatGPT/Search-style retrieval and citations | **GPTBot** |
| **PerplexityBot** | Perplexity search/retrieval | **ClaudeBot** |
| **Claude-SearchBot** | Claude search/retrieval | **CCBot** |
| **ChatGPT-User** | User-triggered fetches/live browsing | **Google-Extended** |
| **Googlebot** | Google search/AI visibility signals | **Applebot-Extended** |
| **Bingbot** | Microsoft/Copilot search visibility | *Some sites also block other training-focused agents separately* |[1][4][8][12][17]

The clearest guidance in the results is to **allow** `OAI-SearchBot`, `Claude-SearchBot`, and `PerplexityBot` for search visibility, and to **disallow** training crawlers such as `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `CCBot`, `Google-Extended`, and `Applebot-Extended` if the goal is to keep content out of model training.[4][17][18][20]

A common robots.txt pattern is:
```txt
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Claude-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: CCBot
Disallow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Disallow: /

User-agent: Applebot-Extended
Disallow: /
``` 
This matches the “allow search, block training” approach described in the sources.[4][17][20]

Two important caveats:
- `robots.txt` is a **policy signal**, not a strong security control; some crawlers may ignore it, so sites that need enforcement should add server-side controls too.[16][20]
- If you use a blanket `Disallow: /`, that blocks *all* crawlers, including the AI search bots you may want to keep visible.[4]

If you want, I can turn this into a **recommended robots.txt** for your specific site goals: **maximize AI search visibility**, **block training**, or **block everything except Google/Bing**.
